summary: On-device evaluation of the pinned shared-session context model (8566382e) on the tap path of the low-RAM emulator. The model runs and reorders every slate, but it cannot satisfy the neural commit gates: at production strength 50 commit decisions are identical to fused on every valid_word row, at strength 100 they remain identical on valid_word while false corrections double elsewhere, and no context-margin commit rule separates confusion targets from wrong promotions (best observed precision ~50% vs the ~95% the gates require).

runs.finding: At the production 35 ms budget the on-device rescore never completes: the deadline circuit breaker opens after a handful of overruns and fused_neural is byte-identical to fused for the rest of the run.

With the deadline lifted the model completes every rescore; the true on-device cost is ~88 ms p50 (~100 ms p95), above both the 35 ms rescorer budget and the 80 ms fused_neural p95 tap gate on this environment.

confusionAnalysis.marginSweep: Flipping the commit to the neural top non-raw candidate whenever its context log-likelihood beats raw's by threshold T yields right/wrong flips of 46/152 (T=0.5), 38/74 (T=2.0), 28/37 (T=3.0); restricting to edit-distance<=1 candidates yields at best 31 right vs 44 wrong (T=2.0). Jointly requiring raw context < -0.8 gives at best 16 right vs 17 wrong. No operating point approaches the ~21 net-correct flips with <=1 added false correction the gates require.

runs.finding: Neural rescoring improves valid_word top-3 (+9.4 pts overall, 31%->47% on confusions) but never moves a valid_word commit: the raw word's fused score keeps rank 1 on every row. On tap_error rows where commits do change, accuracy drops 74%->60%.
Doubling the neural strength to the maximum still cannot flip a single valid_word commit (raw prior always keeps rank 1) while roughly doubling false corrections on tap_error and lexical rows.

neuralContextRelativeErrorReduction.status: unreachable with this model's commit-level precision on this corpus

neuralValidWordAbsoluteGain.status: commit accuracy unchanged at any allowed strength

falseCorrectionIncrease.status: passes only because commits never change

tapP95Latency.status: fails on low_ram_emulator when the rescorer actually completes

peakAddedNeuralMemoryMiB.status: within gate on this run; whole-process upper bound, not an isolated neural peak

limitations: Emulator-only; the GrapheneOS Pixel was not connected during these runs.
400-row diagnostic limit; confusion analysis covers the first 145 should_correct rows.
Latency measured with the diagnostic 500 ms rescorer budget, not the production 35 ms budget.
Memory figure is whole-process PSS minus fixture; it can miss transient peaks.
conclusion: The pinned context model is functional on-device but is not a net improvement on the tap commit path at any permitted strength, matching the negative swipe-slate result. Passing the neural commit gates would require a materially better context model or a redesigned commit policy; neither is achievable inside the pinned artifacts.
